verses.greek: Μὴ πολλοὶ διδάσκαλοι γίνεσθε, ἀδελφοί μου, εἰδότες ὅτι μεῖζον κρίμα λημψόμεθα·
verses.literal: Not many of you teachers do become brothers of mine knowing that greater judgment we will receive.
verses.dgt: Not many of you should become teachers, my brothers and sisters, knowing that we will receive a greater judgment.

verses.greek: πολλὰ γὰρ πταίομεν ἅπαντες. εἴ τις ἐν λόγῳ οὐ πταίει, οὗτος τέλειος ἀνήρ, δυνατὸς χαλιναγωγῆσαι καὶ ὅλον τὸ σῶμα.
verses.literal: In many ways for we stumble all If anyone in what he says not does stumble this one is a perfect man able to bridle indeed all the body.
verses.dgt: For we all stumble in many ways. If anyone does not stumble in word, this one is a mature person, able also to bridle the whole body.

verses.greek: εἰ δὲ τῶν ἵππων τοὺς χαλινοὺς εἰς τὰ στόματα βάλλομεν εἰς τὸ πείθεσθαι αὐτοὺς ἡμῖν, καὶ ὅλον τὸ σῶμα αὐτῶν μετάγομεν.
verses.literal: If now of the horses the bits into the mouths we put for the to obey them us even all the body of them we turn about.
verses.dgt: Now if we put bits into horses’ mouths so that they obey us, we also guide their whole body.

verses.greek: ἰδοὺ καὶ τὰ πλοῖα, τηλικαῦτα ὄντα καὶ ὑπὸ ἀνέμων σκληρῶν ἐλαυνόμενα, μετάγεται ὑπὸ ἐλαχίστου πηδαλίου ὅπου ἡ ὁρμὴ τοῦ εὐθύνοντος βούλεται·
verses.literal: Behold also the ships so great being and by winds strong being driven are turned about by a very small rudder where the impulse of the one who is steering decides.
verses.dgt: Look also at ships: though so large and driven by strong winds, they are guided by a very small rudder wherever the impulse of the one steering wishes.

verses.greek: οὕτως καὶ ἡ γλῶσσα μικρὸν μέλος ἐστὶν καὶ μεγάλα αὐχεῖ. Ἰδοὺ ἡλίκον πῦρ ἡλίκην ὕλην ἀνάπτει·
verses.literal: Thus also the tongue a small member is and exceeding things it boasts. Behold a great fire how great a forest it kindles
verses.dgt: So also the tongue is a small member and boasts great things. Look how small a fire sets ablaze how great a forest.

verses.greek: καὶ ἡ γλῶσσα πῦρ, ὁ κόσμος τῆς ἀδικίας ἡ γλῶσσα καθίσταται ἐν τοῖς μέλεσιν ἡμῶν, ἡ σπιλοῦσα ὅλον τὸ σῶμα καὶ φλογίζουσα τὸν τροχὸν τῆς γενέσεως καὶ φλογιζομένη ὑπὸ τῆς γεέννης.
verses.literal: Also the tongue is a fire the world the of iniquity The tongue is set among the members of us which is defiling all the body and setting on fire the course the of nature and itself being set on fire by the hell.
verses.dgt: And the tongue is a fire, the world of unrighteousness. The tongue is set among our members, staining the whole body, setting on fire the course of life, and itself set on fire by Gehenna.

verses.greek: πᾶσα γὰρ φύσις θηρίων τε καὶ πετεινῶν ἑρπετῶν τε καὶ ἐναλίων δαμάζεται καὶ δεδάμασται τῇ φύσει τῇ ἀνθρωπίνῃ·
verses.literal: All for kinds of beasts both and of birds of creeping things both and things of the sea is subdued and he has been subdued by the race the human
verses.dgt: For every kind of beast and bird, reptile and sea creature, is tamed and has been tamed by humankind,

verses.greek: τὴν δὲ γλῶσσαν οὐδεὶς δαμάσαι δύναται ἀνθρώπων· ἀκατάστατον κακόν, μεστὴ ἰοῦ θανατηφόρου.
verses.literal: the but tongue no one to subdue is able of men it is an unruly evil full of poison deadly.
verses.dgt: but no human being is able to tame the tongue. It is a restless evil, full of deadly poison.

verses.greek: ἐν αὐτῇ εὐλογοῦμεν τὸν κύριον καὶ πατέρα, καὶ ἐν αὐτῇ καταρώμεθα τοὺς ἀνθρώπους τοὺς καθʼ ὁμοίωσιν θεοῦ γεγονότας·
verses.literal: With it we bless the Lord and Father and with it we curse the men those according to the likeness of God having been made
verses.dgt: With it we bless the Lord and Father, and with it we curse people who have been made according to the likeness of God.

verses.greek: ἐκ τοῦ αὐτοῦ στόματος ἐξέρχεται εὐλογία καὶ κατάρα. οὐ χρή, ἀδελφοί μου, ταῦτα οὕτως γίνεσθαι.
verses.literal: Out of the same mouth proceed forth blessing and cursing. Not ought brothers of Mine these things so to be.
verses.dgt: From the same mouth come blessing and cursing. My brothers and sisters, these things ought not to be so.

verses.greek: μήτι ἡ πηγὴ ἐκ τῆς αὐτῆς ὀπῆς βρύει τὸ γλυκὺ καὶ τὸ πικρόν;
verses.literal: surely not ever the spring out of the same opening pours forth the both fresh and the bitter?
verses.dgt: Does a spring pour out from the same opening both sweet and bitter water?

verses.greek: μὴ δύναται, ἀδελφοί μου, συκῆ ἐλαίας ποιῆσαι ἢ ἄμπελος σῦκα; οὔτε ἁλυκὸν γλυκὺ ποιῆσαι ὕδωρ.
verses.literal: Surely not is able brothers of mine a fig tree olives to produce Or a vine figs? Nor of salt fresh to produce water.
verses.dgt: Can a fig tree, my brothers and sisters, produce olives, or a grapevine figs? Neither can salt water produce fresh.

verses.greek: Τίς σοφὸς καὶ ἐπιστήμων ἐν ὑμῖν; δειξάτω ἐκ τῆς καλῆς ἀναστροφῆς τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ ἐν πραΰτητι σοφίας.
verses.literal: Who is wise and understanding among you? he should show out of the good conduct the works of him in the humility of wisdom.
verses.dgt: Who is wise and understanding among you? Let that person show from good conduct their works in the gentleness of wisdom.

verses.greek: εἰ δὲ ζῆλον πικρὸν ἔχετε καὶ ἐριθείαν ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ ὑμῶν, μὴ κατακαυχᾶσθε καὶ ψεύδεσθε κατὰ τῆς ἀληθείας.
verses.literal: If however jealousy bitter you have and self-interest in the heart of you not do boast of it and do lie against the truth.
verses.dgt: But if you have bitter jealousy and selfish ambition in your heart, do not boast and lie against the truth.

verses.greek: οὐκ ἔστιν αὕτη ἡ σοφία ἄνωθεν κατερχομένη, ἀλλὰ ἐπίγειος, ψυχική, δαιμονιώδης·
verses.literal: Not is this the wisdom from above coming down but is earthly unspiritual demonic.
verses.dgt: This is not the wisdom coming down from above, but earthly, natural, demonic.

verses.greek: ὅπου γὰρ ζῆλος καὶ ἐριθεία, ἐκεῖ ἀκαταστασία καὶ πᾶν φαῦλον πρᾶγμα.
verses.literal: Where for jealousy and self-interest exist there will be disorder and every evil thing.
verses.dgt: For where jealousy and selfish ambition are, there is disorder and every worthless practice.

verses.greek: ἡ δὲ ἄνωθεν σοφία πρῶτον μὲν ἁγνή ἐστιν, ἔπειτα εἰρηνική, ἐπιεικής, εὐπειθής, μεστὴ ἐλέους καὶ καρπῶν ἀγαθῶν, ἀδιάκριτος, ἀνυπόκριτος·
verses.literal: the But the from above wisdom first indeed pure is then peaceable gentle reasonable full of mercy and of fruits good impartial sincere.
verses.dgt: But the wisdom from above is first pure, then peaceable, gentle, open to reason, full of mercy and good fruits, impartial, sincere.

verses.greek: καρπὸς δὲ δικαιοσύνης ἐν εἰρήνῃ σπείρεται τοῖς ποιοῦσιν εἰρήνην.
verses.literal: The fruit moreover of righteousness in peace is sown by those making peace.
verses.dgt: And a fruit of righteousness is sown in peace by those who make peace.
